panels.title: Sources OK / total
panels.description: Sources that returned a usable body against sources configured, published once per cycle, so both trail a config edit by a cycle and ok below total means fetch failures that cycle. Instant read: with nothing exported right now the tile is red no-data, which is also every restart before the first published cycle.

panels.title: Last publish age
panels.description: Seconds since the last cycle that PUBLISHED a list, rendered as an age: a cycle that runs and fails does not reset it, so this is how stale the list is, not when the worker last ran. Read as an instant query — nothing exported now reads red whatever the time range, and cannot tell a restart from a dead scrape.

panels.title: Pipeline funnel
panels.description: Last cycle counted through the pipeline, in legend order: merged (unique nodes after dedupe), probed, dead-skipped (never probed — a recent probe found them dead), kept (published). merged = dead-skipped + probed, so the merged-to-probed gap is the dead cache, not loss; probed to kept is the probe plus the gates.

panels.title: Through-node filter drops by reason
panels.description: Nodes each through-node gate dropped, by reason: blocked (service answered, refused this egress), unreachable (never completed through the node), slow (under the bandwidth minimum). A zero line means the gate ran and dropped nobody; no line means it produced no verdict — unconfigured, no usable key, or cancelled.

panels.title: Feeds (both owners): top 25 (last cycle)

targets.expr: sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_nodes_total{job="$job"}) and on(feed, owner) topk(25, sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}))
sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_tested_nodes{job="$job"}) and on(feed, owner) topk(25, sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}))
sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_published_nodes{job="$job"}) and on(feed, owner) topk(25, sum by (feed, owner) (stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}))

panels.description: Per-source counts summed by feed and owner, top 25 ranked on valid. A feed is the channel an entry was minted from, or the entry's own name where none was recorded (metrics.go sourceFeed), so a row folds into one every source the channel it records minted, while an entry that records no channel is its own row -- every curated entry on either instance today, and on the crawler side the inline aggregate and any bare-hash mint. Read this table for the channel view; read it for one entry's total only after checking that entry sets feed. Columns: feed, owner (crawler or curated), then yielded, valid, kept, filtered from nodes_total, valid_nodes, tested_nodes, published_nodes. Both labels come from the exporter, so no name is parsed here.

panels.title: Crawler sources: top 25 (last cycle)
panels.description: Top 25 crawler-managed sources (owner="crawler") ranked on valid, names verbatim: yielded/valid/kept/filtered are nodes_total/valid_nodes/tested_nodes/published_nodes. valid is pre-merge and kept post-merge, so dedup shrinks kept — and this table is not comparable row-for-row with the curated one beside it.

panels.title: Curated sources: top 25 (last cycle)
panels.description: Top 25 hand-curated sources (owner="curated") ranked on valid, names verbatim, same columns as the crawler table. Not comparable row-for-row with it: the curated overlay merges first and Merge is first-wins, so kept and filtered here are inflated against it.

panels.title: Ownership split: crawler vs curated (last cycle)
panels.description: Both owner sides summed into two rows — the exporter's owner label, crawler vs curated — with the tables' columns plus a count of sources that reported last cycle. filtered is ATTRIBUTION, not contribution: the curated overlay merges first and Merge is first-wins, so a shared node is credited to the curated row.

panels.title: Cloudflare egress trace
panels.description: Published nodes split by whether Cloudflare's cdn-cgi/trace answered, plus moved — answered nodes whose measured egress country differs from the one the offline chain assigned. Nothing here drops a node, and moved is counted over answered nodes only, so a large unanswered share makes it less representative.

panels.title: Kept-node speed
panels.description: Download speed of the nodes published last cycle: exact avg and max, plus p50/p90 interpolated from fixed buckets topping out at 500 Mbps, so a quantile pinned at 500 means faster than 500, not a plateau. With no bandwidth filter configured, avg still draws a flat zero while p50/p90 and max vanish.

panels.title: Kept-node latency
panels.description: Mean per-node probe delay in ms over the nodes published last cycle — the value the survivor gate (check.max_avg_ms) admits on and then sorts the list by. Read p90 and max against this job's own threshold: well under it the gate is not binding, pressed against it the cut is sitting inside the live population.

panels.title: Cycle duration, rate & failures
panels.description: Wall time of the last published cycle in seconds on the left axis; cycles and failures counted over a rolling hour on the right. cycles/h counts every attempt, published or failed, so failures/h is a subset of it — and both counters are exported before the first cycle publishes, when duration is still absent.

panels.title: Unresolved GEO tags in published list
panels.description: Published nodes whose GEO tag came out [GEO:??] because no annotation provider resolved a country, as a count on the left axis and a percentage of the published list on the right. These nodes are absent from the per-country metric, so a collapsing annotation chain is visible only here.

panels.title: Cycle time by phase
panels.description: Stacked per-phase wall time, in seconds, of the last cycle that PUBLISHED — an aborted cycle leaves the previous one standing. The unstacked total runs above the stack because the steps between phases belong to no phase, and probe covers the whole Probe call including the TCP pre-check, which has no phase of its own.

panels.title: Probe outcome by stage
panels.description: Where the probe ended for each node probed, stacked to close over probed: condemned (the TCP pre-check refused the server, no URL test spent), connect, fetch, passed, unknown (no result at all — its mapping did not parse and its endpoint was never condemned). A condemned node is also dead-cached for hours, so it leaves the next few cycles' probed count.

panels.title: Top countries in published list (last cycle)
panels.description: Node counts per country over the published list only, top 15 of the last cycle. topk returns a bar solely for countries that have nodes, so a collapsed cycle shows fewer; bar colour is scaled to the largest bar, encoding share of the top country rather than health, and unplaceable nodes are absent from this metric.

panels.title: IP-stage drops by reason
panels.description: Nodes the per-node IP-stage filters dropped in preprocess, summed over every source and split by reason. unsupported is not a filter drop — it counts unparseable input lines, which never entered the fetched total — and a flat zero on geo, asn or cidr may mean the selected job's instance configures no such filter.

panels.title: IP-stage yield
panels.description: Nodes every source yielded against those that survived the IP stage, survival share on the right axis. Both are summed per source before dedupe, so survived normally sits far above merged, equal only when nothing is left to dedupe. "fetched" excludes lines the parser refused, counted as reason=unsupported.

panels.title: TCP pre-check (reachability)
panels.description: What the probe phase's TCP reachability pre-check did, in distinct server:port endpoints — never the condemned NODE count on the probe-outcome panel. trusted = 1: refused endpoints were condemned unprobed and dead-cached; trusted = 0: the breaker rejected the verdict and every node was probed; unresolved fails open.
